281	func TestResolveSessionWorkspace(t *testing.T) {
282		tests := []struct {
283			name              string
284			history           map[string]historyEntry
285			projectWorkspaces map[string]string
286			want              string
287		}{
288			{
289				name:              "history is authoritative over the project mapping",
290				history:           map[string]historyEntry{"conv-1": {Workspace: "/from/history"}},
291				projectWorkspaces: map[string]string{"conv-1": "/from/project"},
292				want:              "/from/history",
293			},
294			{
295				name:              "falls back to the CLI log/config project mapping",
296				history:           map[string]historyEntry{},
297				projectWorkspaces: map[string]string{"conv-1": "/from/project"},
298				want:              "/from/project",
299			},
300			{
301				name:              "a history entry with a blank workspace does not shadow the mapping",
302				history:           map[string]historyEntry{"conv-1": {Workspace: "  "}},
303				projectWorkspaces: map[string]string{"conv-1": "/from/project"},
304				want:              "/from/project",
305			},
306			{
307				// Deliberately NOT inferred from the paths the tools touched: the
308				// common ancestor collapses above the project as soon as one path
309				// falls outside it, which would attach the session to every
310				// unrelated project beneath that ancestor.
311				name:              "no stated workspace yields empty rather than a guess",
312				history:           map[string]historyEntry{},
313				projectWorkspaces: nil,
314				want:              "",
315			},
316		}
317		for _, tt := range tests {
318			t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
319				if got := resolveSessionWorkspace("conv-1", tt.history, tt.projectWorkspaces); got != tt.want {
320					t.Errorf("resolveSessionWorkspace() = %q, want %q", got, tt.want)
321				}
322			})
323		}
324	}
325	
326	// A session with no stated workspace (agy -p print mode) is placed purely by the
327	// paths its tools touched. It must reach the project it actually worked in and
328	// no other — in particular it must not match a sibling project just because both
329	// live under a directory the session also read from.
330	func TestSessionMatchesProject_NoStatedWorkspace(t *testing.T) {
331		home := t.TempDir()
332		projA := filepath.Join(home, "Source", "projA")
333		projB := filepath.Join(home, "Source", "projB")
334		for _, dir := range []string{projA, projB} {
335			if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
336				t.Fatalf("mkdir: %v", err)
337			}
338		}
339		// The files must exist: path matching canonicalizes both sides, and on macOS
340		// the temp root is a symlink, so an absent file cannot be resolved to the
341		// same real path as the project directory it sits in.
342		touched := filepath.Join(projA, "main.go")
343		dotfile := filepath.Join(home, ".zshrc")
344		for _, f := range []string{touched, dotfile} {
345			if err := os.WriteFile(f, []byte("x"), 0o644); err != nil {
346				t.Fatalf("write %s: %v", f, err)
347			}
348		}
349	
350		session := &agSession{
351			Workspace: "",
352			Steps: []transcriptStep{{Type: typePlannerResponse, ToolCalls: []transcriptToolCall{
353				{Name: "view_file", Args: map[string]any{"AbsolutePath": dotfile}},
354				{Name: "view_file", Args: map[string]any{"AbsolutePath": touched}},
355			}}},
356		}
357	
358		if !sessionMatchesProject(session, projA) {
359			t.Errorf("session should match the project whose files it touched")
360		}
361		if sessionMatchesProject(session, projB) {
362			t.Errorf("session must not match a sibling project it never touched")
363		}
364	}

385		}

292	func TestGetAgentChatSession_ToolResultCorrelation(t *testing.T) {

296		// Steps are written in scrambled FILE order to reproduce agy 1.1.x behavior:
297		//   - an async result line (grep, step 4) precedes its call's PLANNER_RESPONSE
298		//     (step 3) — requires step_index sorting, else the result orphans and every
299		//     later pairing shifts by one;
300		//   - within the multi-call step 3 (view_file, grep_search) the results are
301		//     indexed in completion order (grep step 4 before view step 5) — requires
302		//     type-aware routing, else FIFO swaps them;
303		//   - search_web emits a dedicated SEARCH_WEB result type — must be recognized
304		//     by source, not a hardcoded type allowlist, else it is dropped.
305		writeConversation(t, home, "conv-1",
306			`{"step_index":0,"source":"USER_EXPLICIT","type":"USER_INPUT","created_at":"2026-07-24T10:00:00Z","content":"<USER_REQUEST>\ndemo\n</USER_REQUEST>"}`,
307			`{"step_index":1,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","created_at":"2026-07-24T10:00:01Z","tool_calls":[{"name":"list_dir","args":{"DirectoryPath":"/x"}}]}`,

309			`{"step_index":4,"source":"MODEL","type":"GREP_SEARCH","created_at":"2026-07-24T10:00:04Z","content":"GREP-HITS"}`,
310			`{"step_index":3,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","created_at":"2026-07-24T10:00:03Z","tool_calls":[{"name":"view_file","args":{"AbsolutePath":"/x/a.txt"}},{"name":"grep_search","args":{"Query":"foo","SearchPath":"/x"}}]}`,
311			`{"step_index":5,"source":"MODEL","type":"VIEW_FILE","created_at":"2026-07-24T10:00:05Z","content":"FILE-CONTENTS"}`,
312			`{"step_index":6,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","created_at":"2026-07-24T10:00:06Z","tool_calls":[{"name":"search_web","args":{"query":"foo"}}]}`,
313			`{"step_index":7,"source":"MODEL","type":"SEARCH_WEB","created_at":"2026-07-24T10:00:07Z","content":"WEB-RESULTS"}`,
314		)

316		chat, err := NewProvider().GetAgentChatSession("", "conv-1", false)

147	// waitFor polls until *counter reaches want or the test times out, accounting
148	// for the watcher dispatching callbacks on a goroutine.
149	func waitFor(t *testing.T, mu *sync.Mutex, counter *int, want int) {
150		t.Helper()
151		for i := 0; i < 200; i++ {
152			mu.Lock()
153			got := *counter
154			mu.Unlock()
155			if got == want {
156				return
157			}
158			if got > want {
159				t.Fatalf("callback fired %d times, want %d", got, want)
160			}
161			time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
162		}
163		t.Fatalf("callback never reached %d", want)
164	}

- (11) ✅ Exemplary "why" comments — they explain the historical 8-column budget, why long IDs would shove columns out of alignment, and why the floor preserves the old layout. This is the hardest part of the TUI change to understand and the comments carry it

- (16) ❓ Scope creep — this rebrands the accent colors of *all six existing agents* (256-color codes → brand-ish hex values), which is unrelated to adding Antigravity. It also silently changes behavior on terminals without truecolor support (hex colors degrade differently than 256-color indexes). Was this intentional to bundle here, or should it be its own PR?

Since `formatToolInput` dispatches on Antigravity's *real* tool names, whose arg keys are known and PascalCase (per the spec), these aliases can never match — dead flexibility that pads every call site. I'd trim to the observed keys; the generic-JSON fallback already covers surprises

- (75) ⚠️ `formatContentBlock` (line 745) escapes embedded fences as `\``` ` — but backslash is not an escape inside a markdown fence, so a file containing ``` still breaks the block *and* the content is visibly altered. The robust idiom is lengthening the fence (```` ```` ````) instead. Same latent issue applies to diff/text fences elsewhere, so a shared fence helper would fix it once
- (76) ⚠️ `renderGenericJSON` (lines 772-799) hand-builds JSON text ~30 lines to get sorted keys — but `json.MarshalIndent` on a map already emits sorted keys. After deleting the two meta keys, this whole function collapses to a few lines. Prefer the simpler stdlib route ("readable over clever")

**Lines 167-220: `handleWatchEvent`, path helpers**

- (95) ✅ Forgetting removed/renamed dirs from `watchedDirs` so recreations are re-watched shows real fsnotify experience — but it only deletes `event.Name` itself. Deleting all map entries with the removed dir as prefix would close this
- (96) ✅ `processTranscriptFile` re-resolving the *preferred* transcript when an event fires on the fallback file (with the why-comment) prevents emitting stale double-encoded content — and it doubles as a guard against transcript-shaped paths outside `brain/` (tested)

- (99) ✅ Panic recovery around the callback keeps a misbehaving consumer from killing the watcher

---

## Most important improvements

1. **Scope the tab-stripping in `cleanResultContent` to RUN_COMMAND results** (`agent_session.go:378`, observation 59). Today every result type loses all leading tabs on every line, which corrupts tab-indented file contents shown by `view_file` (a viewed Makefile renders semantically broken). Pass the step type through, or only strip the uniform indent that agy actually inserts.

2. **Fix or remove the WAL pragma on the read-only summaries DB** (`project_mapping.go:112-115`, observation 82). A `mode=ro` connection can't set journal mode, so the line doesn't do what its comment claims. Delete it (best-effort error handling already covers contention) or replace with `busy_timeout` if that was the intent.

3. **Clear descendant entries from `watchedDirs` on Remove/Rename** (`watcher.go:176-178`, observation 95). A deleted-then-recreated conversation directory currently leaves stale "already watched" markers for its subdirectories, permanently blinding the watcher to that conversation.

4. **Simplify `renderGenericJSON` to `json.MarshalIndent`** (observation 76) and **use fence-lengthening instead of backslash-escaping embedded ``` ** (observation 75). Both are "readable over clever"/correctness wins in the markdown layer.

5. **Decide whether the agent color-palette overhaul belongs in this PR** (observations 16-18). It rebrands all existing agents' colors and changes light-theme legibility for cursor — worth either splitting out or explicitly owning in the PR description.

Also worth a maintainer decision (not this PR's job): the check/exec helper block is now duplicated across seven providers (observations 31, 89) — a shared `pkg/spi` helper is overdue.

## Unit test assessment

The new tests are the strongest part of the PR — genuinely non-trivial, scenario-driven, and they pin the decisions most likely to regress:

- **Excellent, would catch real bugs**: `TestGetAgentChatSession_ToolResultCorrelation` (provider_test.go:292) is the best test in the PR — scrambled file order, interleaved multi-call results, and a dedicated new result type, each of which fails under a naive implementation (no sorting, pure FIFO, or a result-type allowlist). `TestSessionMatchesProject_NoStatedWorkspace` pins the no-inference workspace decision including the macOS-symlink subtlety (with a comment explaining why files must exist). `TestProcessTranscriptFile_PrefersPrimaryForFallbackEvents` and `_IgnoresTranscriptOutsideBrain` cover real watcher hazards. `TestIndexConversationProjectsFromLog_PendingConversationBeforeProject` pins the either-order log parsing. `TestDeriveModel`'s decimal-point case pins the exact regex subtlety the comment describes.
- **Well-designed contracts**: reconstruct tests pin the unsupported-resume contract; `TestGetAgentChatSession_UnscopedReturnedByID` and `TestListAllAgentChatSessions` pin the unscoped-session policy from both directions; `TestListAgentChatSessions_PrefersSummaryName` covers the full title→preview→derived fallback chain.
- **Reliability**: filesystem tests use `t.TempDir()`/`t.Setenv("HOME", …)`, and `waitFor` polls with a mutex rather than sleeping blind — also failing on *over*-firing (`got > want`). No flakiness concerns. One nit: `TestProcessTranscriptFile_IgnoresTranscriptOutsideBrain` uses a bare 25ms sleep to prove a negative, which is inherently weaker, but acceptable.
- **Data-driven where it matters**: `TestClassifyToolType`, `TestCleanUserPrompt`, `TestResolveSessionWorkspace`, `TestWorkspacesOverlap`, `TestBuildCheckErrorMessage`, `TestEnsureResumeArgs` are all table-driven. `TestRenderInputs`/`TestRenderHighValueInputs` bundle heterogeneous assertions per tool instead of a table — borderline, but each block asserts different structure, so a forced table would obscure more than it saves.
- **Trivial/tautological**: `TestName` (asserts a constant returns itself) adds nothing and could be dropped. `TestMsEpochToRFC3339`'s second assertion only checks non-empty — asserting the exact string would make it meaningful. `TestExpandTilde` is thin but tests real logic.

**Suggested additions** (all target real logic, none for coverage's sake):

- `ensureResumeArgs`: the `--conversation=<id>` and empty `--conversation=` forms are implemented (antigravity_exec.go:81-88) but untested — two more table rows would cover the only untested branch of genuinely fiddly slice logic.
- `cleanResultContent`: a case with legitimately tab-indented content (e.g. a viewed Makefile) — today it would *document* the mangling in observation 59, and after the fix it becomes the regression guard.
- `splitLeadJSON`: a direct case for JSON-followed-by-trailing-garbage (the `break`-keep-partial branch at markdown_tools.go:267-271) — currently only the happy paths are exercised via the subagent formatters.
- `agentColWidth` needs no test (trivial max loop) — correctly left untested per the project's philosophy.

Both items are done, lint is clean (`0 issues`), and all provider tests pass. The changes are left uncommitted on your branch, per your git rules.

**Observation 68 — speculative alias keys** (`markdown_tools.go`)

Each per-tool renderer now reads exactly the arg keys its tool has been observed to emit, sourced from the spec's §3.5 catalog for the file tools (`CommandLine`/`Cwd`, `AbsolutePath`, `DirectoryPath`, `Query`/`SearchPath`, `TargetFile`/`CodeContent`/`TargetContent`/`ReplacementContent`) and from the captured-session test fixtures for the rest (`query` lowercase for `search_web`, `Url`/`Prompt` for `read_url_content`). The invented aliases (`file_path`, `path`, `cmd`, `q`, `uri`, `old_str`, …) are gone. This is safe because every renderer is dispatched by the tool's *real* name — if agy ever renames a key, the renderer finds nothing and falls back to `renderGenericJSON`, which shows the raw args instead of matching a wrong guess. I added a section comment above the renderers stating that principle, including the note that key casing genuinely varies by tool (file tools PascalCase, `search_web` lowercase, `define_subagent`/`ask_question` snake_case), so nobody "fixes" the casing later. Two things I deliberately did **not** touch: `send_message` and `schedule` keep both casing variants of their keys since their args have never been captured verbatim, and `extractPathHints` keeps its lowercase forward-compat list because it runs for *all* tools including MCP tools with unknown shapes.

**Observation 82 — WAL pragma on the read-only DB** (`project_mapping.go`)

The `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` exec (and its misleading comment) is removed. The open stays `sql.Open("sqlite", path+"?mode=ro")` — the same bare-path `mode=ro` form `cursorcli` already uses with this driver, so read-only enforcement is consistent with the codebase. I replaced the comment with one that captures the rationale you gave: this provider never writes Antigravity's data because agy sessions can't be reconstructed for resume (pointing at `reconstruct.go`), so every DB access is read-only and can never corrupt or block a live `agy` writer. This was the only `sql.Open` in the package, so "only ever open r/o" now holds package-wide.

**One bonus fix**: gopls flagged `typeGeneric` in `transcript_parser.go` as declared-but-unused (pre-existing — golangci doesn't run that analyzer, which is why the earlier lint pass was clean). I removed the constant; the `GENERIC` result type is still documented in the const block's comment and handled by `resultStepToolType`'s default case.

Remaining gopls ★ suggestions (`slices.Contains` in `addPathHint`, `SplitSeq` in the split loops) are pre-existing style hints on untouched code and golangci is clean — I left them alone, but they'd be trivial follow-ups if you want them.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-24 20:55:56Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-24 20:55:56Z)**_

Both improvements are in, lint is clean, and the full test suite passes. All changes remain uncommitted on the branch.

**MIP 1 — tab-stripping scoped and made lossless** (`agent_session.go`)

`cleanResultContent` no longer strips all leading tabs from every result. The spec (§3.9) shows agy's shape: unindented `Created At:`/`Completed At:` headers, then a *uniformly* tab-indented output block — and that block's content can carry its own deeper tabs (a `cat Makefile` prints real tab-indented rules). So the new flow is: remove header lines first, then — for RUN_COMMAND results only — call a new `stripSharedTabIndent` that removes just the indent common to every non-blank line, leaving deeper tabs intact. Every other result type (`VIEW_FILE`, `CODE_ACTION`, …) now passes through with its whitespace untouched. One subtlety I hit and fixed: the function had trimmed the whole string up front, which ate the first line's indent and skewed the shared-indent computation to zero — trimming now only happens at the end, with a comment warning about exactly that (the existing `TestBuildExchanges_GroupsAndAttaches` caught it before I did).

**MIP 4 — fence correctness + generic-JSON simplification** (`markdown_tools.go`)

- New `codeFence(lang, body)` helper: the fence is one backtick longer than the longest backtick run inside the body (minimum the standard three), since backslash-escaping backticks inside a fence does nothing. All four fence emitters now use it — `formatToolOutput`'s text block, `formatDiffBlockOutput`, `formatDiffBlock`, and the write-tool content block — so an agent-written markdown file containing its own ``` can no longer break the rendered block, and content is never altered. `formatContentBlock` (whose only job was the broken escaping) is deleted, inlined into `renderWriteInput`.
- `renderGenericJSON` shrank from ~30 hand-built lines to a filter + `json.MarshalIndent` (map keys come out sorted, so determinism is preserved — noted in a comment), and the now-unused `renderJSONValue` and `sort` import are gone.

**Tests added** (`markdown_tools_test.go`): `TestCleanResultContent_TabHandling` pins both sides of MIP 1 — the shared indent stripped while a deeper Makefile tab survives, and `view_file` content passing through byte-identical — and `TestCodeFence_OutrunsEmbeddedBackticks` pins the fence growing past an embedded ```` ``` ```` with the body unaltered, plus the plain three-backtick case. Both would have failed against the old code, so they're genuine regression guards, not tautologies.

Fixed — observation 50 stands corrected in the code. Lint is clean and the provider tests pass.

What changed in `agent_session.go`: `Provider.Version` is now the constant `"unknown"`, matching the five providers that treat the field as the CLI version (Antigravity records no CLI version anywhere in its session data — it's only obtainable live from `agy --version` at check time). The comment on the field now states exactly that, plus the pointer that the model is *not* a substitute because it's carried on each agent message's `Model` field — which was already happening via `convertPlannerStep`, so no model information is lost. `deriveModel` and `session.Model` remain in use for that purpose.

Tests: `TestGenerateAgentSession_Validates` now asserts the model lands on the agent message (`Model == "Gemini 3.5 Flash (High)"`) instead of on `Provider.Version`, and I deleted `TestGenerateAgentSession_UnknownModelFallsBack` since asserting a constant equals itself is exactly the kind of tautological test the project avoids.

One heads-up beyond this PR: `deepseektui` is the origin of the copied pattern — it puts `session.Metadata.Model` in `Version` (`pkg/providers/deepseektui/agent_session.go:191`). That's pre-existing on `dev`, so I left it alone, but it's the same inconsistency if you want it cleaned up separately.

func startIndexWarm(p *tea.Program, projectID string, builtFresh bool) context.CancelFunc {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	if builtFresh {
		return cancel
	}
	dbPath, err := sessionindex.DefaultPath()
	if err != nil {
		slog.Debug("warm: no db path; skipping", "error", err)
		return cancel
	}
	go warmIndexInBackground(ctx, dbPath, projectID, func() { p.Send(indexWarmedMsg{}) })
	return cancel
}

// selectResumeViaTUI runs the picker for the current project and returns the chosen
// resume plan (or nil if the user cancelled). On a successful selection it persists the
// view-mode and target-agent preferences to the user config.
func selectResumeViaTUI(registry *factory.Registry, store *sessionindex.Store, projectID, projectName, presetTo string, builtFresh bool, pinned *sessionindex.Session) (*resumePlan, error) {
	sessions, err := store.ListByProject(projectID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("loading sessions: %w", err)
	}
	// An empty current project is fine — the picker opens in the all-projects browser.
	// Only bail when the whole index is empty (nothing to resume anywhere). A pinned session
	// (--session) is itself something to resume, so skip the bail even on an empty index.
	if pinned == nil {
		if total, _ := store.Count(); total == 0 {
			fprintln(os.Stderr, "\nNo agent sessions indexed yet. Run an agent here, then try again (or `specstory reindex`).")
			return nil, nil
		}
	}

	agents := map[string]agentMeta{}
	var installed []agentChoice
	for _, id := range registry.ListIDs() {
		prov, err := registry.Get(id)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		agents[id] = agentMeta{name: prov.Name(), accent: colorForAgent(id)}
		if prov.Check("").Success {
			installed = append(installed, agentChoice{id: id, provider: prov})
		}
	}
	if len(installed) == 0 {
		fprintln(os.Stderr, "\nNo installed agents found to resume into.")
		return nil, nil
	}

	// A preset target (`resume <agent>`) must be installed to resume into. The command already
	// confirmed it is a known provider; here, with the installed set known, confirm it is
	// available and resolve it to its canonical ID. When set, the picker skips the
	// target-selection step entirely (see beginResume).
	if presetTo != "" {
		resolved := ""
		for _, a := range installed {
			if strings.EqualFold(a.id, presetTo) {
				resolved = a.id
				break
			}
		}
		if resolved == "" {
			return nil, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
				"agent %q is not installed, so it can't be a resume target.", presetTo)}
		}
		presetTo = resolved
	}

	viewMode, lastAgent := "dense", ""
	if cfg, _ := config.Load(nil); cfg != nil {
		viewMode = cfg.GetResumeViewMode()
		lastAgent = cfg.GetResumeLastAgent()
	}

	model := newSessionTUI(store, registry, projectID, projectName, sessions, agents, installed, sessionTUIOpts{
		title:         "SpecStory Resume",
		presetTo:      presetTo,
		lastAgent:     lastAgent,
		viewMode:      viewMode,
		pinnedSession: pinned,
	})

// CreateResumeCommand builds the `specstory resume` command. It opens the interactive
// picker (a Bubble Tea TUI over the sessions.db index — see docs/RESUME-TUI.md): browse
// the current project's sessions across all agents, pick one, choose a target agent, then
// reconstruct (cross-agent) or native-resume (same agent) and launch with auto-save.
func CreateResumeCommand(cloudURL *string, defaults SessionFlagDefaults) *cobra.Command {
	longDesc := `Resume a past coding-agent session — in the same agent, or a different one.

'resume' opens an interactive picker of the sessions in the current project across all agents. Press tab to switch projects. Pick a session, then choose which installed agent to continue it in, and go. Resuming into a different agent reconstructs the conversation into that agent's native format first.

Pass an agent to set the resume target up front, e.g. 'specstory resume codex' — the picker then skips the target-selection step and resumes straight into that agent. The agent must be a known, installed provider, or the command errors.

Pass --session <uri> to resume a specific session without first browsing: a specstory:// URI, a cloud permalink, or a bare session UUID. When you also specify a target agent, you launch right into the resumed session; without a target agent the agent picker opens first.

Resuming SpecStory Cloud sessions (from your other machines) requires an active SpecStory Cloud login + SpecStory Pro.`

	resumeCmd := &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "resume [agent]",
		Short: "Resume a past session, optionally in a different project or agent",
		Long:  longDesc,
		Args:  cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			config.EnsureDefaultProjectConfig()
			slog.Info("Running in resume mode")

			registry := factory.GetRegistry()

			// Optional positional arg pre-selects the target agent (e.g. `resume codex`).
			// An unknown agent name should fail the run rather than be silently ignored, so
			// validate it against the registry up front. When set and valid, the picker skips
			// the target-selection step entirely (see selectResumeViaTUI / beginResume); whether
			// the named agent is actually installed is checked there, where the installed set
			// is known.
			presetTarget := ""
			if len(args) == 1 {

				if _, err := registry.Get(presetTarget); err != nil {

			store, builtFresh, err := openOrBuildResumeIndex()

	if plan.fromID == plan.toID {

		return plan.sessionID, nil
	}

	// One event records every cross-agent reconstruction outcome so portability usage and
	// failure rates are visible. Fired at each terminal branch below.
	track := func(outcome string) {
		analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventResumeReconstructed, analytics.Properties{
			"from_agent": plan.fromID,
			"to_agent":   plan.toID,
			"outcome":    outcome,

	slog.Info("resume: reconstructing cross-agent session",

	// Cross-agent: load source SessionData, reconstruct, write into target store.
	// The source must be read from the directory it was originally launched in, not the
	// user's current cwd — a session picked from another project (all-projects browser)
	// lives elsewhere, and providers like Codex locate it by its recorded cwd. The
	// reconstructed session is still written and launched under the current cwd below.
	fromCwd := plan.fromCwd
	if fromCwd == "" {

	}
	fromSession, err := plan.from.GetAgentChatSession(fromCwd, plan.sessionID, false)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to load source session: %w", err)
	}
	if fromSession == nil || fromSession.SessionData == nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("source session %s has no data to reconstruct", plan.sessionID)
	}

	note := fmt.Sprintf("Resumed from a %s session via SpecStory.", plan.from.Name())
	rec, err := materializeReconstructed(plan, cwd, fromSession.SessionData, note)
	if err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported) {
			track("unsupported")
			return "", utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
				"%s can't yet be a cross-agent resume target. Choose Claude Code or Codex CLI (or resume in %s itself).",
				plan.to.Name(), plan.from.Name())}
		}
		slog.Warn("resume: reconstruction failed", "from", plan.fromID, "to", plan.toID, "error", err)
		track("error")
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to reconstruct session for %s: %w", plan.to.Name(), err)
	}
	track("success")
	fprintf(out, "\nReconstructed %s session into %s as %s.\n", plan.from.Name(), plan.to.Name(), shortID(rec.SessionID))

// prepareCloudResumeTarget resumes a session that lives only in SpecStory Cloud: fetch its
// SessionData, refuse a schema newer than this CLI understands, then reconstruct into the target
// agent's native store (always — there is no local file to resume in place). Returns the fresh
// native session ID, just like the cross-agent path.
func prepareCloudResumeTarget(plan *resumePlan, cwd string, out io.Writer) (string, error) {
	track := func(outcome string) {
		analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventResumeReconstructed, analytics.Properties{
			"from_agent": plan.fromID,
			"to_agent":   plan.toID,
			"outcome":    outcome,
			"source":     "cloud",
		})
	}

	fprintf(out, "\nFetching %s session %s from SpecStory Cloud...\n", plan.from.Name(), shortID(plan.sessionID))
	raw, err := cloud.FetchSessionData(plan.projectID, plan.sessionID)
	if err != nil {
		track("error")
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to fetch session from cloud: %w", err)
	}

	var data schema.SessionData
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &data); err != nil {
		track("error")
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to parse cloud session data: %w", err)
	}

	// Refuse a blob produced by a newer CLI schema than this build understands — reconstructing it
	// could silently drop or mangle fields this version doesn't know about.
	if schemaVersionNewer(data.SchemaVersion, schema.CurrentSchemaVersion) {
		track("schema_too_new")
		return "", utils.ValidationError{Message: "Resuming this session requires an updated SpecStory CLI."}
	}

	note := fmt.Sprintf("Resumed from a %s session on another machine via SpecStory.", plan.from.Name())
	rec, err := materializeReconstructed(plan, cwd, &data, note)
	if err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported) {
			track("unsupported")
			return "", utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
				"%s can't yet be a resume target. Choose Claude Code or Codex CLI.", plan.to.Name())}
		}
		slog.Warn("resume: cloud reconstruction failed", "from", plan.fromID, "to", plan.toID, "error", err)
		track("error")
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to reconstruct cloud session for %s: %w", plan.to.Name(), err)
	}
	track("success")
	fprintf(out, "Reconstructed cloud %s session into %s as %s.\n", plan.from.Name(), plan.to.Name(), shortID(rec.SessionID))
	printCursorIDERestartNote(plan, out)
	return rec.SessionID, nil
}

// printCursorIDERestartNote tells the user how to surface a session reconstructed into Cursor
// IDE's store: Cursor only picks up imported sessions from its SQLite database on startup, so
// unlike CLI targets the result is not visible until the app is restarted.
func printCursorIDERestartNote(plan *resumePlan, out io.Writer) {
	if plan.toID == "cursoride" {
		fprintf(out, "\nNote: only Cursor 3 is supported. Restart Cursor to see the imported session in the Agent sidebar.\n")
	}
}

		WorkspaceRoot: cwd,

}

// beginResume advances from a chosen session toward launch. When a target agent was
// pre-selected via `resume <agent>`, that choice is honored immediately and the picker exits
// — the user is never asked to pick a target. Otherwise it moves to the target-selection step.
func (m sessionTUI) beginResume(sess *sessionindex.Session) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
	m.chosen = sess
	if m.presetTo != "" {
		m.result = sessionTUIResult{session: sess, targetID: m.presetTo}
		return m, tea.Quit
	}
	return m.enterTargetPicker(sess), nil
}

// enterTargetPicker pins sess as the chosen session and opens the target-selection step, with
// the highlight on the last-resumed agent (else the session's own agent). Shared by the
// picker's selection flow (beginResume) and the --session pinned entry, so the two can't drift.
func (m sessionTUI) enterTargetPicker(sess *sessionindex.Session) sessionTUI {
	m.chosen = sess
	m.mode = modeTarget
	m.targetCursor = m.defaultTargetIndex()
	return m
}

func (m sessionTUI) defaultTargetIndex() int {
	// Prefer the last-resumed agent, else the chosen session's own agent (same-agent resume).
	// An explicit preset (`resume <agent>`) never reaches here — beginResume skips the
	// target-selection step entirely in that case.
	want := m.lastAgent
	if want == "" && m.chosen != nil {
		want = m.chosen.Agent
	}
	for i, a := range m.installed {
		if a.id == want {
			return i
		}
	}
	return 0
}

func (m sessionTUI) renderTarget() string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString(styBold.Render("Resume into which agent?"))
	if m.chosen != nil {
		b.WriteString(styDim.Render("   " + sessionTitle(*m.chosen)))
	}
	b.WriteString("\n\n")
	for i, a := range m.installed {
		cursor := "   "
		label := a.provider.Name()
		// The "native resume" hint applies only to local sessions. A cloud session has no local
		// native file, so even the same agent reconstructs — show no extra label there.
		if m.chosen != nil && a.id == m.chosen.Agent && !m.chosen.IsCloud {
			label += styFaint.Render(" (same agent — native resume)")
		}
		if i == m.targetCursor {
			cursor = styCursor.Render(" ▸ ")
			label = stySel.Render(a.provider.Name()) + label[len(a.provider.Name()):]
		}
		b.WriteString(cursor + label + "\n")
	}
	b.WriteString("\n")
	b.WriteString(styDim.Render(strings.Join([]string{"↑↓ move", "↵ resume", "esc back"}, " · ")))
	return b.String()
}

// renderDeleteConfirm draws the y/N soft-delete confirmation, spelling out that the delete hides

===target keys===
func (m sessionTUI) updateTarget(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
	switch msg.String() {
	case "esc", "q":
		m.mode = modeList
		m.chosen = nil
	case "ctrl+c":
		m.result = sessionTUIResult{cancelled: true}
		return m, tea.Quit
	case "up", "k":
		if m.targetCursor > 0 {
			m.targetCursor--
		}
	case "down", "j":
		if m.targetCursor < len(m.installed)-1 {
			m.targetCursor++
		}
	case "enter":
		m.result = sessionTUIResult{session: m.chosen, targetID: m.installed[m.targetCursor].id}
		return m, tea.Quit
	}
	return m, nil
}

50	//
51	// Rules (per the locked design):
52	//   - user/agent text content -> a turn of that role
53	//   - thinking content -> folded into the agent turn's text (not dropped)
54	//   - tool calls -> folded into the agent turn's text via the pre-rendered
55	//     Summary / FormattedMarkdown captured on the forward pass

80				if strings.TrimSpace(text) == "" {
81					continue
82				}
83	
84				// Drop synthetic, non-conversational turns (slash-command invocations,
85				// local-command output, etc.) so they are not replayed into the resumed
86				// session. This is intentionally reconstruction-only — archival markdown
87				// stays faithful to the source session.
88				if isSyntheticTurnText(text) {
89					continue
90				}
91	
92				turns = append(turns, Turn{Role: msg.Role, Text: text})
93			}
94		}
95	
96		return turns
97	}
98	
99	// PrepareTurns validates session data and flattens it into the neutral turn list
100	// every provider's serializer consumes. It centralizes the two guards each
101	// ReconstructSession must apply before it can build native output: the source
102	// SessionData must be non-nil, and flattening must yield at least one turn.
103	// Keeping these here means every provider rejects the same cases with the same
104	// messages and cannot drift apart.
105	func PrepareTurns(data *schema.SessionData, opts ReconstructOptions) ([]Turn, error) {
106		if data == nil {
107			return nil, errors.New("cannot reconstruct nil session data")
108		}
109	
110		turns := FlattenSessionData(data, opts.MigrationNote)
111		if len(turns) == 0 {
112			return nil, errors.New("session has no content to reconstruct")
113		}
114	
115		return turns, nil
116	}
117	
118	// ResolveWorkspaceRoot picks the working directory a reconstructed session
119	// belongs to: the explicit target from opts when set, otherwise the source
120	// session's own recorded root. Providers derive native paths/IDs from the
121	// result; the cursor provider is the lone exception that needs no workspace.
122	func ResolveWorkspaceRoot(opts ReconstructOptions, data *schema.SessionData) string {
123		if opts.WorkspaceRoot != "" {
124			return opts.WorkspaceRoot
125		}
126		if data == nil {
127			return ""
128		}
129		return data.WorkspaceRoot
130	}
131	
132	// reconstructMillisLayout is the RFC 3339 millisecond layout with a literal Z that the
133	// Claude Code, Codex, Droid, and Gemini serializers stamp on reconstructed records.
134	// (DeepSeek uses microsecond precision and formats its own.)
135	const reconstructMillisLayout = "2006-01-02T15:04:05.000Z"
136	
137	// RFC3339Millis formats t with millisecond precision and a literal Z, the timestamp shape
138	// shared by the Claude/Codex/Droid/Gemini serializers. Callers pass a UTC time.
139	func RFC3339Millis(t time.Time) string {
140		return t.Format(reconstructMillisLayout)
141	}
142	
143	// ResumedSessionTitle returns the display title for a reconstructed session: the trimmed
144	// source slug, or "Resumed session" when the slug is blank or whitespace-only. Centralizing
145	// this keeps the trim (which a couple of serializers previously skipped) and the fallback
146	// consistent across providers.
147	func ResumedSessionTitle(slug string) string {
148		if title := strings.TrimSpace(slug); title != "" {
149			return title
150		}
151		return "Resumed session"
152	}
153	
154	// ReconstructRole maps a flattened Turn role to the "user"/"assistant" role string used by
155	// most native session formats. Providers with a different role vocabulary (e.g. Gemini's
156	// "gemini", Codex's event labels) map their own.
157	func ReconstructRole(role string) string {
158		if role == schema.RoleUser {
159			return "user"
160		}
161		return "assistant"
162	}
163	
164	// SyntheticCommandTags are the wrapper tags coding agents inject for
165	// non-conversational slash-command records: the command invocation, its piped
166	// local stdout/stderr, and the local-command caveat. They are conversation
167	// scaffolding, never a real user prompt. This is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for
168	// the tag set, shared by reconstruction's turn filter here (matched anywhere in a
169	// flattened turn) and Claude Code's title-selection filter
170	// (claudecode.isSyntheticMessage, matched as a leading tag), so the two cannot
171	// drift apart.
172	var SyntheticCommandTags = []string{
173		"<command-name>",
174		"<command-message>",
175		"<command-args>",
176		"<local-command-stdout>",
177		"<local-command-stderr>",
178		"<local-command-caveat>",
179	}
180	
181	// extraSyntheticTurnMarkers are synthetic markers beyond the shared command tags
182	// that must also never be replayed into a resumed session: Claude Code's
183	// <TEXTBLOCK> title-generation wrapper and its interrupt marker (which also has a
184	// "…for tool use" variant, caught by the prefix).
185	var extraSyntheticTurnMarkers = []string{
186		"<TEXTBLOCK>",
187		"[Request interrupted by user",
188	}
189	
190	// isSyntheticTurnText reports whether a flattened turn is a synthetic,
191	// non-conversational artifact that should not be replayed into a resumed session.
192	// It matches by Contains because a flattened turn concatenates content parts, so a
193	// marker can appear anywhere in the text. Markdown generation does NOT use this
194	// filter and stays faithful to source.
195	func isSyntheticTurnText(text string) bool {
196		for _, marker := range SyntheticCommandTags {
197			if strings.Contains(text, marker) {
198				return true
199			}
200		}
201		for _, marker := range extraSyntheticTurnMarkers {
202			if strings.Contains(text, marker) {
203				return true
204			}
205		}
206		return false
207	}
208	
209	// messageTurnText flattens a single message into its turn text: all text/thinking
210	// content parts joined, followed by the tool's pre-rendered markdown when present.
211	func messageTurnText(msg *schema.Message) string {
212		var parts []string
213	
214		for _, part := range msg.Content {
215			// Both "text" and "thinking" parts carry their content in Text; thinking
216			// is intentionally treated as ordinary agent text.
217			if strings.TrimSpace(part.Text) != "" {
218				parts = append(parts, part.Text)
219			}
220		}
221	
222		text := strings.Join(parts, "\n\n")
223	
224		if msg.Tool != nil {
225			toolText := toolTurnText(msg.Tool)
226			if toolText != "" {
227				if text != "" {
228					text += "\n\n" + toolText
229				} else {
230					text = toolText
231				}
232			}
233		}
234	
235		return text
236	}
237	
238	// toolTurnText renders a tool call as agent text, reusing the markdown the
239	// forward pass already produced (Summary + FormattedMarkdown). Falls back to a
240	// minimal description when neither is available.
241	func toolTurnText(tool *schema.ToolInfo) string {
242		var b strings.Builder
243	
244		if tool.Summary != nil && strings.TrimSpace(*tool.Summary) != "" {
245			b.WriteString(strings.TrimSpace(*tool.Summary))
246		}
247	
248		if tool.FormattedMarkdown != nil && strings.TrimSpace(*tool.FormattedMarkdown) != "" {
249			if b.Len() > 0 {
250				b.WriteString("\n\n")
251			}
252			b.WriteString(strings.TrimRight(*tool.FormattedMarkdown, "\n"))
253		}
254	
255		if b.Len() == 0 {
256			// Nothing pre-rendered; emit a minimal, non-empty description so the tool
257			// activity is at least acknowledged in the transcript.
258			b.WriteString("Tool use: " + tool.Name)
259		}
260	
261		return b.String()
262	}
263
```

func TestFTSQuery(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct{ name, in, want string }{
		{"empty", "", ""},
		{"single word is a prefix", "thank", "thank*"},
		{"bare words are independent prefixes", "thank you", "thank* you*"},
		{"punctuation in a bare word splits into an adjacency phrase", "max-cpu!", "max + cpu*"},
		{"a bare filename is an adjacency phrase with prefix last", "poem.txt", "poem + txt*"},
		{"a quoted filename is a committed phrase, no prefix", `"poem.txt"`, `"poem txt"`},
		{"an open-quoted filename keeps the last token a prefix", `"poem.txt`, "poem + txt*"},
		{"closed phrase is exact adjacency", `"thank you"`, `"thank you"`},
		{"closed single-word phrase has no prefix", `"thank"`, `"thank"`},
		{"open phrase keeps last word a prefix", `"thank yo`, "thank + yo*"},
		{"open single-word phrase is a prefix", `"thank`, "thank*"},
		{"phrase plus trailing bare word", `"thank you" now`, `"thank you" now*`},
		{"bare word before a closed phrase", `please "thank you"`, `please* "thank you"`},
		{"whitespace inside a phrase is collapsed", `"thank    you"`, `"thank you"`},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if got := ftsQuery(c.in); got != c.want {
				t.Errorf("ftsQuery(%q) = %q, want %q", c.in, got, c.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestBeginResumeWithPresetSkipsTargetStep(t *testing.T) {
	sess := &sessionindex.Session{SessionID: "s1", Agent: "codex"}
	m := sessionTUI{presetTo: "claude"}

	next, cmd := m.beginResume(sess)
	rm := next.(sessionTUI)

	if cmd == nil {
		t.Error("expected an immediate quit command when a target is preset")
	}
	if rm.mode == modeTarget {
		t.Error("a preset target must skip the target-selection step")
	}
	if rm.result.session != sess {
		t.Errorf("result session = %v, want the chosen session", rm.result.session)
	}
	if rm.result.targetID != "claude" {
		t.Errorf("result target = %q, want %q", rm.result.targetID, "claude")
	}
}

// TestBeginResumeWithoutPresetEntersTargetStep verifies the default flow: with no preset,
// choosing a session advances to the target-selection step (no immediate resume).
func TestBeginResumeWithoutPresetEntersTargetStep(t *testing.T) {
	sess := &sessionindex.Session{SessionID: "s1", Agent: "codex"}
	m := sessionTUI{}

	next, cmd := m.beginResume(sess)
	rm := next.(sessionTUI)

	if cmd != nil {
		t.Error("expected no immediate quit without a preset target")
	}
	if rm.mode != modeTarget {
		t.Errorf("mode = %v, want modeTarget", rm.mode)
	}
	if rm.chosen != sess {
		t.Error("chosen session must be recorded before target selection")
	}
}

Done — both dumb behaviors from your transcript are fixed, with the session-aware filtering you picked. Lint clean, all tests pass, and the rebuilt `./specstory` confirms the immediate error.

**What changed:**

- **`pkg/spi/reconstruct.go`** — new `SupportsReconstruction(p Provider) bool`: probes `NativeSessionPath`, which providers without a native serializer answer with `ErrReconstructionUnsupported`. It's a pure path computation for every provider, so the capability check has no side effects and no hardcoded agent list.

- **`pkg/cmd/session_tui.go` / `session_tui_view.go`** — the target step now shows `m.targets`, computed per chosen session by `eligibleTargets`: every reconstruction-capable agent, plus the session's *own* agent when the session is local (native in-place resume — which is why Antigravity still appears for local agy sessions, from any project). Cloud sessions and other agents' sessions never list it. Both entry points (picker selection and `--session` pinned) flow through `enterTargetPicker`, so one computation covers both. If nothing qualifies (only agy installed + a cloud session), the step renders "No installed agent can resume this session." and Enter is a no-op.

- **`pkg/cmd/resume.go`** — `specstory resume antigravity` now fails immediately, before the picker opens:

  ```
  ERROR  Antigravity CLI can't be a resume target for other agents' sessions.
  Run 'specstory resume' without a target and pick one of its own sessions to resume in place.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-24 21:59:03Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-24 21:59:14Z)**_

That feedback is wrong on the facts — I'd reject it.

`delete` on a nil map is explicitly defined as a no-op in Go (spec: "if the map m is nil or does not contain such an element, delete is a no-op"). It never panics. So the flagged line is already safe against exactly the scenario the feedback describes — a `watchState` constructed without `watchedDirs`. The tests in `watcher_test.go` actually do construct `&watchState{lastProcessed: make(map[string]int64)}` with a nil `watchedDirs`, and that's fine.

The only version of the concern that's real is a nil `*watchState` pointer itself — but a nil-check for that would be defending against a caller bug that can't happen: every path into `handleWatchEvent` comes from `watchSessions`, which builds the state via `newWatchState()`. Guarding an internal helper against an impossible nil is exactly the kind of speculative defensiveness the codebase conventions push back on ("verify the code has to exist").

If the reviewer wanted a genuine hazard in that neighborhood, there are two better targets:

1. **The write side, not the delete side**: `addWatch` does `state.watchedDirs[dir] = true` — assigning into a nil map *does* panic. That's the line that would bite someone constructing ad-hoc state in a test. It doesn't today because the tests that skip `newWatchState` never reach the watch-setup path, but if anything deserved hardening (or just a comment saying "construct via newWatchState"), it's that.

2. **The actual bug on the flagged line** — still open as MIP 3 from my review: `delete(state.watchedDirs, event.Name)` only forgets the removed directory *itself*. If `brain/<id>` is deleted and recreated, its descendants (`.system_generated`, `logs`) stay marked as watched, so `addConversationWatches` skips re-adding them and the recreated conversation is never watched again. The fix is deleting every entry with the removed path as a prefix — a real behavioral fix, versus the feedback's cosmetic one.

So: the panic claim is incorrect, the proposed nil-check is noise, but the line it points at does deserve a change — just a different one. Want me to do the MIP 3 fix while we're here?

Verdict: **this one's right — accept it.** The reviewer's premise checks out empirically, and it exposed that the format spec is incomplete.

Your real transcripts on this machine contain dedicated result-step types the spec's §3.2 "all observed values" table doesn't list: `SEARCH_WEB`, `READ_URL_CONTENT`, `GENERATE_IMAGE`, `INVOKE_SUBAGENT`, and `ASK_QUESTION` all appear (once each, alongside the seven documented types). So the code's own artifacts were contradicting each other — the correlation test comment claimed `SEARCH_WEB` is real, the spec said tools without a dedicated type produce `GENERIC` — and the transcripts side with the test.

Given that, the feedback's mechanical point stands: `resultStepToolType` sends these observed types to `default: ""` → pure FIFO. Concretely, with pending calls `[run_command, search_web]` and the web search completing first (searches are often faster than commands), the `SEARCH_WEB` result attaches to `run_command` — exactly the mispairing the type-aware routing exists to prevent. The comment on `resultStepToolType` frames returning `""` for these as a deliberate choice, but that choice was justified only while the types were hypothetical; they're observed now.

What accepting it should look like:

- Map `SEARCH_WEB`, `READ_URL_CONTENT` → `schema.ToolTypeSearch` and `GENERATE_IMAGE`, `INVOKE_SUBAGENT`, `ASK_QUESTION` → `schema.ToolTypeGeneric` (matching what `classifyToolType` gives their originating calls), with new named constants. `GENERIC` itself should stay `""` — it's ambiguous by definition, and `pickPendingTool`'s any-type fallback still covers it.
- Update spec §3.2 with the five newly observed rows, so "all observed values" is true again.
- Add a focused routing test: `SEARCH_WEB` result skipping an older pending `run_command` to reach the pending `search_web` — the scenario FIFO gets wrong.

One nuance worth noting when replying to the reviewer: the granularity is the SpecStory tool *type*, not the tool name — so `grep_search` and `search_web` both map to `search` and can still mispair with each other under concurrent completion. That's inherent to the existing design (VIEW_FILE/LIST_DIRECTORY share `read` the same way), and the mapping still strictly dominates FIFO.

Want me to implement it?

Valid — accept this one too. It's a smaller cousin of the arg-key issue: hardcoded text that stops being true the moment a custom command is configured.

Verified in `provider.go`: the `version_failed` branch of `Check` passes the *resolved* binary path into `buildCheckErrorMessage` (`provider.go:59`), and the other two branches already use it — the `not_found` custom case prints "Provided command: %s" and the permission case prints `chmod +x %s`. Only the `default:` branch ignores its `command` parameter and hardcodes `` `agy --version` `` twice (`provider.go:346,352`). So with `antigravity_cmd = "~/bin/agy-wrapper"`, a version-probe failure tells the user to run `agy --version` — a command that may not even exist on their PATH, while the actual failing binary goes unnamed. The fix is exactly what the reviewer says: render `command` + the `versionFlag` const in both lines.

Two side notes:

- The existing test keeps guarding it for free: `TestBuildCheckErrorMessage`'s `version_failed` case passes `command: "agy"` and wants the substring `"agy --version"`, which the parameterized message still produces.
- This is another instance of the seven-times-duplicated check-helper block (observation 31) — the siblings almost certainly hardcode their own binary names the same way. Fixing antigravity here is right for this PR; the rest belongs to the eventual shared-helper refactor.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-24 22:09:18Z)**_

This one's a real find — **accept, but the proposed fix is only a third of what's actually needed.** The reviewer spotted the gap but not its full depth.

**The gap is genuine.** The provider's own design creates it: `statusRunning`'s comment says agy "writes the eventual output to a sidecar task log **rather than rewriting the step**". So when a long async command finishes: the output lands in `.system_generated/tasks/task-N.log`, the transcript is untouched, and the watcher — which watches only `<id>`, `.system_generated`, and `logs/` — hears nothing. During a live `specstory run antigravity`, the final output of an async command won't appear in the markdown until something else touches the transcript (next turn). The `tasks/` dir creation *is* seen (its parent `.system_generated` is watched), but `addConversationWatches` never adds it as a level, so writes inside are invisible.

**But "also watch tasks/" alone does nothing**, because two more layers filter the event out:

1. **The path filter** — `handleWatchEvent` drops anything that isn't `isTranscriptPath()`, so a `task-34.log` write event would be discarded even from a watched dir. It needs a companion `isTaskLogPath` check (parent dir `tasks`, name `task-*.log`).
2. **The mtime dedup** — `emitConversation` keys change detection on the *transcript's* mtime (`last >= file.ModTime` → skip). A task-log-only update leaves the transcript mtime unchanged, so the re-emit would be suppressed anyway. The change-detection timestamp needs to incorporate the task log (e.g. use the triggering task log's mtime, or max over transcript + task logs).

One thing that happily *doesn't* need changing: `conversationIDFromTranscriptPath` works unmodified for task paths, since `brain/<id>/.system_generated/tasks/task-N.log` has the same depth as the transcript path.

So my verdict for the reviewer thread: correct observation, real live-watch gap, and the fix should be scoped as three coordinated changes (watch the `tasks/` level in `addConversationWatches`, accept task-log paths in `handleWatchEvent`, and widen `emitConversation`'s freshness key) — otherwise the naive version ships a watch that fires events straight into two filters that discard them, which would *look* fixed in the diff and change nothing in behavior.

Severity-wise it's moderate: sync and any subsequent transcript write self-heal (parseTranscript folds task outputs in whenever it runs), so it's a liveness issue for one scenario, not data loss. Worth fixing in this PR since the watcher's whole job is liveness.

Want me to implement the full three-part version?

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-24 22:12:34Z)**_

All three parts are in — lint clean, tests pass.

**Part 1 — watch the `tasks/` level** (`watcher.go`, `addConversationWatches`): each conversation now gets a fourth watch level, `<id>/.system_generated/tasks`, with a comment explaining why it matters (a finished async command appends there *without* rewriting the transcript's RUNNING step, so the task-log write is the only filesystem signal). The `"tasks"` string is now a shared `tasksDirName` constant in `path_utils.go`, also adopted by `loadTaskOutputs`, which had it hardcoded. Since `tasks/` may be created mid-session, its parent `.system_generated` watch sees the dir Create, `setupWatches` re-runs, and the new level gets picked up — the existing level-by-level machinery handles it with no extra code.

**Part 2 — let task-log events through the filter** (`handleWatchEvent` + new `isTaskLogPath`): events now pass if the path is a transcript *or* a `tasks/task-<step>.log` file (prefix/suffix match, parent dir must be `tasks`). `conversationIDFromTranscriptPath` needed no change — task paths sit at the same depth, now noted in its comment.

**Part 3 — widen the freshness key** (`processTranscriptFile`): when the triggering event is a task log, its mtime is folded into the `ModTime` used for dedup (max with the transcript's). Without this, `emitConversation` would compare the unchanged transcript mtime against the already-recorded value and silently drop the re-emit — the trap that would have made a parts-1-and-2-only fix look done while changing nothing. The parameter is renamed `eventPath` to reflect that it's no longer necessarily a transcript.

**Tests**: `TestIsTaskLogPath` covers the classifier (right name in right dir, right name in *wrong* dir, wrong name in right dir). `TestProcessTranscriptFile_TaskLogUpdateReEmits` is the end-to-end guard: transcript with a RUNNING `run_command` emits once; then `task-2.log` appears with `BUILD OK` (mtime bumped explicitly via `os.Chtimes` so the test doesn't depend on filesystem tick resolution), the task-path event fires, and the assertion verifies the *re-emitted* session's tool output now contains the async result. That test fails at the "callback never reached 2" stage against the old code.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-24 22:15:38Z)**_

Copilot is right, and it caught me in an error — my "pure path computation for every provider" claim was wrong. I verified: `geminicli.NativeSessionPath` explicitly documents that "unlike the Claude/Codex resolvers, [it] prepares the project directory" — for a project Gemini has never seen, it calls `prepareGeminiProjectDir`, which `MkdirAll`s `~/.gemini/tmp/<basename>/`, writes a `.project_root` marker, and creates `chats/`. I only read the first few lines of that function when I checked purity earlier and missed the prepare branch below.

The consequence is real and new: since `eligibleTargets` probes every installed provider, merely opening the resume target picker (or running `resume gemini`) in a project Gemini has never touched now creates a phantom Gemini project dir in `~/.gemini/tmp`. That mutation didn't happen before my change, because nothing called `NativeSessionPath` until an actual Gemini-targeted resume.

One part of the feedback I'd still reject: the nil-`Provider` guard is the same speculative-nil noise as the earlier watcher feedback — providers come from the registry and are never nil, and a nil interface would panic long before this call.

For the fix, three options:

1. **Explicit capability method on `spi.Provider`** — add `SupportsReconstruction() bool` to the interface: seven providers `return true`, antigravity `return false`, probe deleted. ~8 trivial implementations plus the test fake. The decisive advantage: it's compiler-enforced, so the *next* provider without a serializer must answer the question explicitly instead of silently re-inheriting the dead-end-target bug. (Recommended)
2. **Inverted marker interface** — antigravity implements an optional `interface{ ReconstructionUnsupported() }`; smallest diff, but the default for a future non-capable provider is wrongly "capable", which is exactly the failure mode we just fixed.
3. **Make gemini's `NativeSessionPath` pure** — moves the dir-prep elsewhere, but `ReconstructSession` is contractually data-only and the caller is provider-agnostic, so the marker logic has no good home; biggest churn, weakest payoff.

Want me to go with option 1?

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-24 22:19:11Z)**_

Done — option 1 is in, the probe is gone, and the full suite (21 packages) passes with lint clean.

**What changed:**

- **`pkg/spi/provider.go`** — `SupportsReconstruction() bool` is now part of the `Provider` interface. Its doc comment encodes both lessons from this thread: it must agree with `ReconstructSession`/`NativeSessionPath` returning `ErrReconstructionUnsupported`, and it must be a *pure capability answer with no filesystem access* — explicitly noting that probing `NativeSessionPath` is not a substitute because some implementations prepare directories (the Gemini side effect Copilot caught).

- **`pkg/spi/reconstruct.go`** — the probing `SupportsReconstruction(p Provider)` helper is deleted.

- **All 8 providers** — each `reconstruct.go` gained the method: seven `return true` with a comment pointing at their serializer, and antigravity `return false` with the why (no serializer produces a session `agy` would actually resume, so it must never be offered as a cross-agent/cloud target). Since the method is on the interface, the compiler now forces every future provider to answer explicitly — a new provider without a serializer can't silently reappear in target lists, and antigravity's existing `var _ spi.Provider` assertion verified its implementation at compile time.

- **Callers** — `eligibleTargets` (session_tui.go) and the preset check (resume.go) now call `provider.SupportsReconstruction()` directly; the no-longer-needed `spi` import in session_tui.go is removed.

- **Tests** — `fakeProvider` answers `!f.reconstructUnsupported`, keeping it consistent with its error-returning methods; `TestSupportsReconstruction` now pins the method on the real registry (and gained a `gemini: true` row, since Gemini was the provider whose probe behavior started this).

Net effect: opening the resume picker no longer touches `~/.gemini` state at all — no probe calls, no phantom project dirs — and the behavior from the session-aware filtering work is unchanged. The nil-guard part of Copilot's feedback I left out, as discussed: registry providers are never nil, and a guard there would be dead code.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-24 22:26:15Z)**_

The diagnosis is technically correct — on Windows, `url.Parse("file:///C:/Users/x").Path` is `"/C:/Users/x"` and `file://server/share` parses the host out of the path — but my recommendation is **defer it, and when Windows lands, fix it by hoisting, not by patching `stripFileURI`**. Here's the reasoning:

**The codebase already contains the correct implementation.** `cursoride/workspace.go:643-696` has a full file-URI → OS-path converter that handles exactly what the feedback asks for — the Windows leading-slash-before-drive-letter trim, `filepath.FromSlash`, and host handling (including WSL `file://wsl.localhost/...` URIs, which the feedback didn't even think of). So the right eventual fix for antigravity is a DRY one: extract that converter into `pkg/spi` and have `stripFileURI` delegate to it — not hand-roll a third URI parser in `antigravitycli`. If this feedback gets applied as written, the codebase ends up with two divergent Windows-URI implementations.

**Why not do the hoist in this PR:**

1. **Untestable against reality.** Every byte of the Antigravity format spec was observed on macOS. Whether Windows agy even emits `file://` URIs, with what casing, drive-letter form, or UNC shapes, is unverified. This PR has now twice removed speculative code written for unobserved data shapes (the phantom tool renderers pre-review, the alias arg keys in this session) on the principle that unverifiable handling "reads as though it were verified behavior." Windows URI handling written today is the same thing.

2. **It's not the load-bearing gap.** The feedback says this "will break workspace/path matching on Windows" — true, but so will `canonicalizePath`, the `HOME`-based store resolution, the symlink/case handling in `pathWithin`, and the tests' `t.Setenv("HOME", ...)` fixtures. `stripFileURI` is one plank in a bridge that doesn't exist yet; fixing it alone ships dead code and a false sense of Windows-readiness.

3. **The "harmless on Unix" assumption isn't quite true.** Trimming the leading slash from paths matching `/X:/...` corrupts a legitimate (if weird) Unix directory literally named `/C:`. Absurd, but it means the change has negative expected value on the two platforms actually supported today.

So for the reviewer thread: acknowledge the bug as real-for-Windows, note it's deliberately out of scope per the project's current no-Windows rule, and file it against the Windows port with the specific remedy — *share cursoride's converter via `pkg/spi` rather than extending `stripFileURI` in place, and validate against real Windows agy captures* (UNC, drive letters, and WSL shapes). If you'd like, I can add a short "why" comment on `stripFileURI` stating it intentionally handles only POSIX file URIs and pointing at cursoride's converter as the shared implementation to adopt — so the Windows port doesn't rediscover this from scratch.

// pathToFileURI converts an absolute filesystem path to a file:// URI.
// Cursor stores workspaceIdentifier.uri.external in percent-encoded form (e.g.
// spaces as %20), so raw string concatenation would produce a URI that doesn't
// match what Cursor writes for paths containing reserved characters, which can
// mis-associate reconstructed sessions with their workspace.
func pathToFileURI(path string) string {
	u := url.URL{Scheme: "file", Path: path}
	return u.String()
}

// uriToPath converts a workspace URI to a local file path.
// Handles standard file:// URIs, WSL file://wsl.localhost/ URIs,
// vscode-remote://wsl+distro/ URIs used by Cursor/VS Code in WSL,
// vscode-remote://ssh-remote+config/path URIs for SSH remotes, and
// vscode-remote://tunnel+host/path URIs for remote tunnels.
func uriToPath(uri string) (string, error) {
	// Handle vscode-remote:// URIs before url.Parse because Go's URL parser
	// rejects percent-encoded characters like %2B in the host component
	// (e.g., vscode-remote://wsl%2Bubuntu/home/user/project)
	if strings.HasPrefix(uri, "vscode-remote://") {
		return parseVSCodeRemoteURI(uri)
	}

	// Parse the URI
	parsedURI, err := url.Parse(uri)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to parse URI: %w", err)
	}

	// Reject non-file schemes
	if parsedURI.Scheme != "file" && parsedURI.Scheme != "" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("unsupported URI scheme %q: %s", parsedURI.Scheme, uri)
	}

	// Get the path from the URI and decode it
	// This converts %3A to : and other URL-encoded characters
	path, err := url.PathUnescape(parsedURI.Path)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to decode URI path: %w", err)
	}

	// Handle WSL file:// URIs (e.g., file://wsl.localhost/Ubuntu/home/user/project)
	// Host is "wsl.localhost" and path starts with /{DistroName}/...
	// Strip the distro name to get the actual WSL filesystem path
	if strings.EqualFold(parsedURI.Host, "wsl.localhost") || strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(parsedURI.Host), "wsl$") {
		// path = /Ubuntu/home/user/project → strip /Ubuntu → /home/user/project
		if len(path) > 1 {
			if idx := strings.Index(path[1:], "/"); idx >= 0 {
				path = path[idx+1:]
				slog.Debug("Converted WSL file URI to path", "uri", uri, "path", path)
				return path, nil
			}
		}
		return "", fmt.Errorf("malformed WSL URI path: %s", uri)
	}

	// On Windows, URL paths have an extra leading slash (e.g., file:///c:/Users becomes /c:/Users)
	// We need to remove the leading slash and normalize the path
	if filepath.Separator == '\\' {
		// Remove leading slash on Windows
		if len(path) > 0 && path[0] == '/' {
			path = path[1:]
		}
		// Normalize path separators to backslashes
		path = filepath.FromSlash(path)
	}

	return path, nil
}

// collectCodeWorkspaceFolders reads a .code-workspace JSON file and returns the
// canonicalized paths of every folder it lists. Used when the project path passed
// in is itself a .code-workspace file, so workspace entries opened directly from
// one of its folders can also be matched (Method 4 in FindAllWorkspacesForProject).
func collectCodeWorkspaceFolders(workspaceFilePath string) []string {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(workspaceFilePath)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Debug("collectCodeWorkspaceFolders: failed to read workspace file",
			"path", workspaceFilePath, "error", err)
		return nil
	}

	var workspace struct {
		Folders []struct {
			Path string `json:"path"`
		} `json:"folders"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &workspace); err != nil {
		slog.Debug("collectCodeWorkspaceFolders: failed to parse workspace file",
			"path", workspaceFilePath, "error", err)
		return nil
	}

	workspaceDir := filepath.Dir(workspaceFilePath)
	var folders []string
	for _, folder := range workspace.Folders {
		if folder.Path == "" {
			continue
		}

		// Resolve relative paths against the workspace file's directory.
		var resolved string
		if filepath.IsAbs(folder.Path) {
			resolved = folder.Path
		} else {
			resolved = filepath.Join(workspaceDir, folder.Path)
		}

		canonical, err := normalizePathForComparison(resolved)
		if err != nil {
			canonical = filepath.Clean(resolved)
		}
		folders = append(folders, canonical)
	}

	return folders
}

// codeWorkspaceContainsFolder checks whether any folder entry in a .code-workspace
// JSON file resolves to canonicalFolder. This is used to find workspaces that were
// opened via a .code-workspace file referencing the target folder.
func codeWorkspaceContainsFolder(workspaceFilePath, canonicalFolder string) bool {
	for _, folder := range collectCodeWorkspaceFolders(workspaceFilePath) {
		if folder == canonicalFolder {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// parseVSCodeRemoteURI extracts the filesystem path from a vscode-remote:// URI.
// Handles three types of remote URIs:
// 1. WSL: vscode-remote://wsl%2B{distro}/{path} - path is the WSL filesystem path
// 2. SSH: vscode-remote://ssh-remote%2B{config-hex}/{path} - path is the remote filesystem path
// 3. Tunnel: vscode-remote://tunnel%2B{host}/{path} - path is the remote filesystem path
// Go's url.Parse rejects %2B in the host component, so we parse manually.
func parseVSCodeRemoteURI(uri string) (string, error) {
	// Strip scheme prefix: "vscode-remote://"
	remainder := strings.TrimPrefix(uri, "vscode-remote://")

	// Split host from path at the first unencoded slash after the host
	// The host is percent-encoded (e.g., "wsl%2Bubuntu" or "ssh-remote%2B{config-hex}")
	slashIdx := strings.Index(remainder, "/")
	if slashIdx < 0 {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("malformed vscode-remote URI (no path): %s", uri)
	}

	host := remainder[:slashIdx]
	pathPart := remainder[slashIdx:]

	// Decode the host to determine remote type
	decodedHost, err := url.PathUnescape(host)
	if err != nil {
		decodedHost = host
	}

	hostLower := strings.ToLower(decodedHost)

	// Check if it's a supported remote type: each host is either bare ("wsl") or
	// carries a "+{config}" suffix ("wsl+ubuntu", "ssh-remote+{config-hex}").
	supportedHosts := []string{"wsl", "ssh-remote", "tunnel", "dev-container"}
	supported := false
	for _, host := range supportedHosts {
		if hostLower == host || strings.HasPrefix(hostLower, host+"+") {
			supported = true
			break
		}
	}
	if !supported {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("unsupported vscode-remote host %q: %s", decodedHost, uri)
	}

	// Decode the path portion
	path, err := url.PathUnescape(pathPart)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to decode vscode-remote URI path: %w", err)
	}

	// Log the conversion with appropriate context
	switch {
	case strings.HasPrefix(hostLower, "ssh-remote"):
		slog.Debug("Converted vscode-remote SSH URI to path", "uri", uri, "path", path)
	case strings.HasPrefix(hostLower, "tunnel"):
		slog.Debug("Converted vscode-remote tunnel URI to path", "uri", uri, "path", path)
	case strings.HasPrefix(hostLower, "dev-container"):
		slog.Debug("Converted vscode-remote dev container URI to path", "uri", uri, "path", path)
	default:
		slog.Debug("Converted vscode-remote WSL URI to path", "uri", uri, "path", path)
	}

	return path, nil
}

// FileURIToPath converts a file:// URI to a local filesystem path, decoding
// percent-escapes (file:///tmp/my%20file.go → /tmp/my file.go). It is the
// single URI→path converter shared by providers whose stores record file URIs
// (Cursor IDE workspace identifiers, Antigravity tool args and project
// configs), so the non-POSIX forms are translated identically everywhere:
//
//   - WSL URIs (file://wsl.localhost/<distro>/path, file://wsl$/...): the host
//     and distro segment are stripped, yielding the in-distro POSIX path.
//   - Drive-letter URIs (file:///C:/Users/...): on Windows the spurious
//     leading slash is trimmed and separators converted (C:\Users\...).
//   - UNC URIs (file://server/share/...): on Windows the host becomes the UNC
//     root (\\server\share\...). On POSIX systems a host has no filesystem
//     meaning and is dropped.
//
// Returns an error for unparseable URIs and schemes other than file.
func FileURIToPath(uri string) (string, error) {
	parsed, err := url.Parse(uri)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to parse URI: %w", err)
	}
	if parsed.Scheme != "file" && parsed.Scheme != "" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("unsupported URI scheme %q: %s", parsed.Scheme, uri)
	}

	path, err := url.PathUnescape(parsed.Path)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to decode URI path: %w", err)
	}

	// WSL URIs carry the distro as the first path segment under a wsl host;
	// the usable path is what remains inside the distro.
	if strings.EqualFold(parsed.Host, "wsl.localhost") || strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(parsed.Host), "wsl$") {
		if len(path) > 1 {
			if idx := strings.Index(path[1:], "/"); idx >= 0 {
				slog.Debug("Converted WSL file URI to path", "uri", uri, "path", path[idx+1:])
				return path[idx+1:], nil
			}
		}
		return "", fmt.Errorf("malformed WSL URI path: %s", uri)
	}

	if filepath.Separator == '\\' {
		// A non-WSL host names a UNC share.
		if parsed.Host != "" {
			return `\\` + parsed.Host + filepath.FromSlash(path), nil
		}
		// Drive-letter URI paths arrive with a spurious leading slash (/C:/Users).
		return filepath.FromSlash(strings.TrimPrefix(path, "/")), nil
	}

	return path, nil
}
EOF

// TestFileURIToPath covers the shared file-URI converter on the POSIX forms
// (the Windows drive-letter/UNC branches are separator-gated and can only run
// on a Windows build; cursoride's TestUriToPath_WindowsPaths documents them).
func TestFileURIToPath(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		uri     string
		want    string
		wantErr bool
	}{
		{name: "plain posix path", uri: "file:///tmp/project/main.go", want: "/tmp/project/main.go"},
		{name: "percent escapes decoded", uri: "file:///tmp/my%20file.go", want: "/tmp/my file.go"},
		{name: "wsl.localhost strips host and distro", uri: "file://wsl.localhost/Ubuntu/home/u/proj", want: "/home/u/proj"},
		{name: "wsl host without in-distro path is malformed", uri: "file://wsl.localhost/Ubuntu", wantErr: true},
		{name: "non-wsl host dropped on posix", uri: "file://server/share/dir", want: "/share/dir"},
		{name: "non-file scheme rejected", uri: "https://example.com/x", wantErr: true},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got, err := FileURIToPath(tt.uri)
			if tt.wantErr {
				if err == nil {
					t.Fatalf("FileURIToPath(%q) = %q, want error", tt.uri, got)
				}
				return
			}
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("FileURIToPath(%q) unexpected error: %v", tt.uri, err)
			}
			if got != tt.want {
				t.Errorf("FileURIToPath(%q) = %q, want %q", tt.uri, got, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
}
EOF

Hoist complete — lint clean, full suite green (21 packages, 0 failures).

**What changed:**

- **`pkg/spi/path_utils.go`** — new `spi.FileURIToPath(uri) (string, error)`: the single file-URI → OS-path converter. It's cursoride's proven logic hoisted intact (parse, percent-decode, WSL `wsl.localhost`/`wsl$` host+distro stripping, Windows drive-letter leading-slash trim + `filepath.FromSlash`) plus the one piece Copilot's original feedback asked for that cursoride lacked: UNC handling — on Windows a non-WSL host becomes the `\\server\share` root. On POSIX, hosts are still dropped, matching historical behavior, and the Windows branch stays separator-gated dead code until the port lands. Error messages were kept verbatim so cursoride's existing error-substring tests still hold.

- **`cursoride/workspace.go`** — `uriToPath` now handles only the Cursor-domain `vscode-remote://` forms and delegates everything else to `spi.FileURIToPath`. Its ~50-line file-URI body is gone; `TestUriToPath` and `TestUriToPath_WindowsPaths` pass unchanged through the delegation, which is the parity proof for the hoist.

- **`antigravitycli/agent_session.go`** — `stripFileURI` keeps its contract (non-URI values pass through untouched, raw `TrimPrefix` fallback on unparseable input) but delegates conversion to the shared helper, so antigravity now inherits WSL handling today and drive-letter/UNC handling the moment a Windows build exists. The now-unused `net/url` import is dropped.

- **Tests** — new `TestFileURIToPath` in `pkg/spi/path_utils_test.go` covers the POSIX-reachable behavior: plain paths, percent-escapes, WSL host+distro stripping, malformed WSL URIs, host-dropped-on-POSIX, and non-file scheme rejection. The Windows branches can't execute on darwin (separator-gated), which the test comment states, pointing at cursoride's Windows table as their documentation.

Net for the reviewer thread: the feedback's scenario is now handled once, centrally — and the codebase went from two divergent URI parsers (about to be three) down to one, with cursoride's WSL knowledge and the new UNC handling shared by every provider that touches file URIs.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-24 22:36:54Z)**_

The diagnosis is correct — it matches observation 34 from my original review — but of the two remedies offered, the streaming one should be rejected and the comment/rename one applied. Here's the reasoning:

**Right:** the constant's comment claims it bounds "JSONL sidecar scanning" in a file whose main job is transcript parsing, yet `parseTranscript` uses `os.ReadFile` + `bytes.Split` and never touches it. Its only real users are the `bufio.Scanner`s for `history.jsonl` and the CLI logs. Name and comment mislead.

**Wrong remedy:** switching `parseTranscript` to a capped `bufio.Scanner` would make things *worse*, not better:

- A scanner with a 16MB cap introduces a new failure mode the current code doesn't have: one line over the cap makes `scanner.Err()` return `ErrTooLong` and aborts the parse, losing every step after it. Today an arbitrarily long line just gets handed to `json.Unmarshal` and parses fine. "Enforcing the limit" on transcripts converts a working case into a lost session.
- The memory claim is overstated. `wantRawData=true` callers (sync, by-id fetch) retain the whole file as `RawData` regardless — streaming saves nothing there. For listing paths (`wantRawData=false`), the transient buffer is one transcript at a time, processed sequentially, at conversation-log scale (KBs–MBs; agy compacts long histories with CHECKPOINTs). There's no realistic high-memory scenario.

So the honest fix is the feedback's own fallback option: make the constant tell the truth. Applying:

Accepted and fixed — lint clean, provider tests pass (the `FileURIToPath` diagnostic is the same stale LSP artifact from earlier; the compiler and golangci are happy).

**The fix** (`agent_session.go`): a third fallback tier — when both the caller's `workspaceRoot` and `session.Workspace` are empty, `WorkspaceRoot` falls back to `os.Getwd()`. The comment now tells the truth in full: it names the exact reachable case (unscoped text-only session loaded by id through a reindex ref with empty `OriginCwd`), why cwd is the honest choice (the schema requires the field, and for a session whose workspace is unknowable the CLI's own directory is the only one there is), and why it's safe (project attribution derives from the ref, never from this field).

**The test** (`TestGenerateAgentSession_UnscopedFallsBackToCwd`): both inputs empty → `WorkspaceRoot` equals cwd *and* `data.Validate()` passes. The validation assertion is the meaningful one — it fails against the old code with the schema's "workspaceRoot is required" complaint.

One parity note: `deepseektui/agent_session.go:166-169` has the byte-for-byte identical two-tier fallback with the same theoretical hole. Whether it's *reachable* there depends on whether DeepSeek session files can lack `Metadata.Workspace` while also being loaded with an empty path — I haven't verified that, and it's pre-existing on `dev`, so I left it. Happy to check and mirror the fix if you want it in this branch, like we did for the `Version` field.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-24 22:47:14Z)**_

Checked — the hole is reachable in deepseektui too, so I mirrored the fix.

**The verification**: DeepSeek's `ListAllAgentChatSessions` sets `OriginCwd: extractWorkspaceFast(file.Path)` (`provider.go:351`), and `extractWorkspaceFast` returns `""` when a session file has no `metadata.workspace` — the provider's own defensive handling shows it doesn't assume the field exists. A ref with empty `OriginCwd` then flows through the same `reindex.go:658` path into `generateAgentSession("", …)`, where `Metadata.Workspace` is also empty — producing the same schema-violating empty `WorkspaceRoot`.

**The mirror** (`deepseektui/agent_session.go`): identical cwd fallback as the final tier, with the same comment structure adapted to DeepSeek's specifics (`metadata.workspace` instead of the resolved workspace). Both providers now resolve `WorkspaceRoot` with the exact same three-tier policy: session's own workspace → caller's project → CLI cwd.

**The test**: rather than a new test function, the existing table (`TestGenerateAgentSession_MetadataWorkspaceAndUsage`) gained a "both empty → cwd" row — it already parameterized `metadataWorkspace`/`callerWorkspace`/`wantWorkspace`, so the new case is three lines plus a `Getwd` at setup. It fails against the old code with an empty `WorkspaceRoot`.

Lint clean, both provider packages pass. (The `interface{}`→`any` hints in the diagnostics are pre-existing gopls suggestions on untouched deepseektui test lines.)

Even if task-*.log events are watched/handled, emitConversation deduplicates purely by the transcript file's ModTime. When only a task log changes, preferred transcript ModTime stays the same so the session won't be re-emitted, and async output won't appear in live autosave. Consider including the task log ModTime in the emitted conversation's ModTime when the triggering event is a task log.

This one's already done — it's exactly "part 3" of the three-part task-log fix from earlier in this session. Copilot is reviewing the stale pre-fix code (the snippet it quotes no longer exists in your working tree; the comment predates the local changes, which are still uncommitted).

The current `processTranscriptFile` does precisely what the reviewer asks:

```go
modTime := info.ModTime().UnixNano()

// A task-log write does not touch the transcript, so fold the log's own
// mtime into the freshness key — otherwise emitConversation would dedupe
// this event against the unchanged transcript mtime and drop the update.
if isTaskLogPath(eventPath) {
    if taskInfo, err := os.Stat(eventPath); err == nil {
        if t := taskInfo.ModTime().UnixNano(); t > modTime {
            modTime = t
        }
    }
}
```

And it's pinned by `TestProcessTranscriptFile_TaskLogUpdateReEmits`, which fails without this exact widening: the transcript emits once, then a `task-2.log` with a bumped mtime arrives, and the test asserts the session re-emits with the async output folded in — the dedup-suppression scenario Copilot describes is the one the test reproduces.

Worth noting Copilot got the *analysis* right independently — it's the same conclusion I reached when assessing the earlier "watch tasks/" feedback: watching the directory alone is inert without letting task-log paths through the event filter *and* widening the freshness key. This comment confirms the third leg was necessary; it just arrived after the work was done.

So: agree with the reviewer, resolve as already-fixed, and once this branch's local changes are pushed, the comment thread can point at `watcher.go`'s `processTranscriptFile` and the new test. No code change needed.
